Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

follow verb

go or come after

also come after, go after, follow me, it follows that

classical

Plaut. Rud. 184b–c: Sequere mē hāc ergō. — Sequor.
Sen. Ep. 107.8: noctem diēs sequitur

sequor, sequī, secūtus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent

follow, go or come after

With the accusative, of people and of what comes after in time. In argument, sequitur ut … is “it follows that …” (Cic. Fat. 28, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Sequere mē hāc ergō. — Sequor.

    Follow me this way, then. — Coming.Plaut. Rud. 184b–c

  • dextrae sē parvus Iūlus implicuit sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs

    little Iulus took hold of my right hand and followed his father with shorter stepsVerg. A. 2.723–724

  • nūbilō serēna succēdunt; turbantur maria cum quiēvērunt; flant invicem ventī; noctem diēs sequitur

    clear skies come after cloud; the seas are stirred up when they have been calm; the winds blow by turns; day follows nightSen. Ep. 107.8

Other words

  • īnsequor, īnsequī, īnsecūtus sum — follow hard after; chase

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Verg. A. 5.321 (Lewis & Short)

  • subsequor, subsequī, subsecūtus sum — follow close behind

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.14: nōn longē itaque Latīna subsequī dēbent

See also follow, do you get it?.
